name: FTC Consumer Alerts
title: The FTC is not calling to deactivate your phone number
text:
Here’s the latest twist on FTC impersonators: someone claiming to be an FTC official (who’s really a scammer) calls to say a phone was registered under your name and number and is being used to commit scams in another country. The “FTC official” even reads off their badge ID (it’s a fake badge). If you don’t cooperate, they threaten to deactivate your phone number. Sounds scary? That’s (unfortunately) the point.
To keep making the story sound real, the FTC impersonator will transfer you to a (fake) police officer to file a report. If you hesitate, they might have you call back the police department directly. They’ll tell you what to search online to find the number. It feels like you’re verifying the story, but it’s all part of their scheme. And when you call, people involved in the scam pick up.
They ask for your ID and other personal information for your “report” and tell you to keep everything secret. Later, you get more bad news: They claim you’re under arrest for the scams your phone number was associated with — and they say you have to go to another country. Unless you send money for a security deposit.
None of this is true — it’s all a scam.
A real FTC employee will never ever reach out to ask you to send money, and will never connect you to someone who says to send money. That’s a scam.
A real FTC employee will never ever threaten to disconnect your phone. That’s a scam.
A real FTC employee will never ever tell you to keep your conversations secret. That’s always a scam.
A real FTC employee will never ever text you a photo of their employee ID to “verify” their identity.
Learn more about how to spot and avoid scammers who pretend to be from the government. Spot one of these scams? Tell the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
